quote: There’s no life / that couldn’t be immortal / if only for a moment. / Death / always arrives by that very moment too late.
source: Wisława Szymborska, ‘On Death, Without Exaggeration’, lines 40 to 44 (trans. Stanisław Barańczak and Clare Cavanagh, 1995)

evidence.where: Full poem text on poetseers.org (Nobel poets library), counted line by line: 48 lines, the quotation is lines 40 to 44 across a stanza break after moment; wording agrees with the Barańczak and Cavanagh text reprinted widely and in Nothing Twice. Harcourt 1995 page not opened.
evidence.edition: View with a Grain of Sand: Selected Poems, trans. Stanisław Barańczak and Clare Cavanagh (Harcourt Brace, 1995); Polish in Ludzie na moście (1986)

reason: Wording, lineation and the proposed line numbers all check against an independent full text of the Barańczak and Cavanagh translation. Not shipped; Szymborska would reach her third line of the year, and the held carry-in 10-poet-14 is also hers, so only one can land this month.
